title: Seat a 4-tooth comb busbar in three DIN breakers, cap its spare tooth, torque each terminal screw to its 2.0 N m click
instruction: Put the grey cap on the comb busbar's spare tooth, seat its other three teeth in the three breakers' top terminals, and tighten each terminal screw with the torque driver until it clicks, then let go of the comb and keep both hands still and clear of it.
context: The hard parts: the comb is one rigid part whose three teeth (18 mm pitch, 1.5 x 10.5 mm) must enter three breakers' top terminals at once, each through a 2.5 x 12.5 mm slot, so it must be square to the row and on all three mouths together; then each terminal is closed onto its tooth and tightened to the breaker maker's 2.0 N m, read by the torque limiter's click. A pinch on the T-handle carries under 1 N m, so for the last turn the other hand pushes its free arm while the first pushes back. Electricians (about 821,000 US jobs in 2025, BLS; O*NET 47-2111: 'Connect wires to circuit breakers, transformers, or other components') bridge rows of breakers with comb busbars and cap the spare teeth. Unlike tasks that snap a module onto a DIN rail, switch breakers or click-torque one bolted lug, here three teeth enter three terminals together before each is closed to the maker's torque.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. Our fixture: a 35 mm steel DIN rail (WAGO 210-113, 9 cm) screwed to a 10 mm steel plate 10 x 10 cm that leans back 30 degrees (so the terminal screws face the arms), welded to a 4 mm steel foot plate with a 6 mm strut behind it. On the rail, three Schneider Electric Acti9 iC60N 1P C16 breakers (A9F74116, or the A9F77116 now sold with the same body), side by side, the middle one's front foot edge at x = 25.5, y = 4.0, 4.0 over the bench; their top terminals open: each screw is closed on a 1.5 mm gauge strip until the driver clicks and turned back half a turn (the clamp plate 1.9 mm off the slot's back wall). A 4-module (72 mm) piece of the Acti9 A9XPH112 comb busbar rests on a poplar rack at x = 35.0, y = 24.5 (its top 4.0 over the bench, at the same 30-degree lean), two posts between its teeth. An Acti9 A9XPT920 tooth cap stands in a poplar holder at x = 29.0, y = 20.5 (floor 3.4 over the bench, leaning 30 degrees). A Wera 416 R T-handle bitholder with a Bernstein 4-985 torque adapter (2.0 N m) and a Wera PZ 2 x 25 mm bit lies in a poplar holster, the T-handle's centre at x = 20.5, y = 10.0, 11.2 over the bench, the bit pointing 30 degrees down towards the panel and the T-handle's arms level along y.
scoring: 0 for good if the comb, the cap or the driver leaves the bench (its centre 1 cm under the bench top). Otherwise read at the end, with every loose part still for 1.0 s (under 10 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s) and both grippers 30 mm or more from the comb: a tooth stands in every breaker's slot at least 22 mm deep (the bar within 4 mm of the tops, the tooth within 1.2 mm of the slot's middle front to back and 3 mm along the row) and each terminal's clamp plate is closed on its tooth, else 0. Then 1.0 if every screw was tightened until the driver's limiter clicked at 2.0 N m and the cap is on the comb's spare tooth; 0.5 if a screw was left short of its click or the spare tooth is bare. On the bench: each click from the trial's video and sound; a tooth seated when the bar rests on the breakers' tops, by eye; a clamp closed when the comb does not lift at a light pull; the cap from the video.
reset_notes: Between trials, about 2 minutes: turn each screw back one turn with the driver, lift the comb out and set it on its rack, pull the cap off the tooth and stand it in its holder; close each screw on a 1.5 mm gauge strip until the driver clicks and turn it back half a turn; put the driver back in its holster, T-handle level.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX; breakers, rail and fixture are one fixed body. A screw turns while the driver's bit is in its hole and the driver turns about the screw's axis (4 deg play in the recess); its plate moves 0.8 mm a turn (the simulated lead: M5 coarse pitch). Torque 0.1 N m free, then 7.3 N m/rad on the tooth, on the driver against its turn (eased in over 0.15 s); at 2.0 N m the limiter slips, its click counted after 3 deg. Welds: the cap on at 22 mm; the clamped comb to the panel.
